input:
In this tutorial passage, we will explore the affinity laws for a centrifugal pump, which are a set of useful relationships that describe how flow, head and power vary with the speed of the pump. By the end of the passage, you will be able to state all three relationships and apply them to a simple worked check: when the speed of a pump doubles, its flow doubles, its head rises fourfold, and its power rises eightfold.

The first relationship concerns flow: the flow through a centrifugal pump varies in direct proportion to its speed, so if you double the speed, the impeller passes twice the volume in the same time and the flow doubles accordingly. The second relationship concerns head, which varies with the square of the speed: the impeller throws the liquid out faster in proportion to the speed, and the energy imparted to each unit of liquid grows with the square of that velocity, meaning that doubling the speed multiplies the head by four. The third relationship concerns power, which varies with the cube of the speed; interestingly, this is not really a separate rule, but rather follows from the two relationships before it, because power is the product of flow and head, the flow carries one factor of speed and the head carries two, and the product therefore carries three. Doubling the speed thus multiplies the power by 8, which serves as a helpful worked check that the three laws are consistent with one another.

Finally, it is important to keep the conditions of the laws in mind when applying them: they compare one pump at two speeds, moving the same liquid, at corresponding points of its characteristic, and they are not a comparison between different pumps, nor do they say anything about whether the system the pump feeds will accept the higher flow. Used within those conditions, the three proportionalities allow a known duty point to be moved to a new speed without the need for a new test.
